question: Which organic leavener is used in the baking industry to make bread, pastries and cakes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Yeasts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Yeasts** are single-celled fungi widely used as a natural leavening agent in baking.
 
• They convert sugars into carbon dioxide and ethanol through the process of **fermentation**, causing dough to rise.
 
• Commonly used yeast species in baking include **Saccharomyces cerevisiae**.
 
• Yeasts are essential in making bread, pastries, and cakes as they improve texture, flavor, and volume.
 
• They are also used in other industries, such as brewing and bioethanol production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fermentation:**

 
 
• A metabolic process where microorganisms like yeast convert carbohydrates into alcohol or acids.
 
• In baking, fermentation produces carbon dioxide, which causes dough to expand and rise.
 
 
 
• **Saccharomyces cerevisiae:**
 
 
• Commonly known as baker's yeast, it is a species of yeast used in baking, brewing, and winemaking.
 
• It is known for its efficiency in sugar fermentation and its ability to produce high-quality products.
 
 
 
• **Leavening agents:**
 
 
• Substances used in baking to produce gas and expand dough or batter.
 
• Types include biological (yeast), chemical (baking powder and soda), and physical (air and steam).
 
 
 
• **Role of yeast in baking:**
 
 
• Yeast fermentation enhances the flavor of baked goods by producing secondary metabolites.
 
• It contributes to the light, airy texture of bread and other baked goods.
